chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) secondary to diabetic nephropathy with resistant hypertension, being evaluated for kidney transplantation.
history_of_present_illness: The patient has experienced progressive decline in renal function over the past several years, advancing from CKD stage 1 in 2017 to stage 4 by mid‑2025. Diabetes mellitus (treated with insulin) and essential hypertension have driven the renal deterioration. Anemia of chronic disease requiring epoetin, osteoporosis, and knee osteoarthritis have added to his morbidity. He continues to smoke daily, consumes alcohol at unhealthy levels, reports ongoing intimate‑partner abuse and high stress. He is currently on a triple antihypertensive regimen, insulin, alendronate, levothyroxine, vitamin B12, nicotine patch, and naproxen while awaiting kidney transplantation. Recent visits show frequent medication reviews and attempts at tobacco cessation, but blood pressure, BMI, eGFR, and lipid data are missing.

active_problems.name: Proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus
